verdict.rationale: Figma Make is built around an in-product AI agent. Users describe what they want in chat and the agent generates apps, creates backends, and adds records. It supports parallel chats, an editable plan before generation, and annotations that give the agent element-level instructions. A community commenter independently confirms that Make's AI writes the React code. Missing for 10: independent hands-on evidence of how reliably the agent completes complex multi-step delegated tasks.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: Describe what you want to build in the chat, and Make can create a Payload-powered backend, including a database, file storage, authentication, and an admin panel.
You can run more than one chat at the same time in a single Make file, so you can start a new change while another chat is still working.
Add [annotations](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/42009840449175#h_01M30Q06FXE1CSX4XT91NBD0A4) to your Make preview to give the agent instructions for specific elements
Clarify intent and create a structured, editable plan before generation starts.
You can ask Make to add sample records so you have content to work with.
